identity.description: SendGrid (Twilio SendGrid) is a cloud email delivery service with a v3 REST API for sending transactional and marketing email, plus templates, contacts, stats, suppressions, billing and email validation. It is owned by Twilio.
identity.identity_notes: Docs at twilio.com/docs/sendgrid describe the Twilio SendGrid v3 API, its API keys, Event Webhook and SDKs. Matches the assigned sendgrid.com hint; sendgrid.com now redirects to twilio.com/en-us/sendgrid.

auth.token_refresh: None documented; keys are static until deleted. Deleting a key stops calls made with it.
auth.scopes_notes: Keys carry permissions: Full Access, Custom Access (per-endpoint, per-access-level), Billing Access, and Email Address Validation Access. A key cannot exceed the creating account's permissions. Billing calls need a separate key.

access.production_restrictions: Not established. Free-plan API access and daily send limits were not confirmed; pricing pages did not load their plan details.

api.limitations: Breadth is only partly established: the sources confirmed the v3 REST pattern, a templates example and permission groups, but not a full endpoint list. Resource-level read/write operations were not verified. SMTP sending is not covered here.

claims.value: API key sent as Bearer token in Authorization header
claims.quote: include an Authorization header with the value Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY_HERE> in your request.

claims.value: API keys are created in the account console
claims.quote: You can create API keys in your account

claims.value: A key cannot have more permissions than the creating user
claims.quote: You can't give an API key greater permissions than your own.

claims.value: Full Access, Custom Access, Billing Access, Email Address Validation Access
claims.quote: Grants all API endpoints full access to your account.

claims.value: Billing calls need a separate API key
claims.quote: To make billing-related API calls, Twilio requires a separate API key.

claims.value: Accounts are limited to 100 API keys
claims.quote: Twilio limits accounts to 100 API keys.

claims.value: Basic auth with username/password is not supported; key-as-password Basic auth is mentioned for some services
Event Webhook sends delivery, engagement and account events
claims.quote: When Twilio SendGrid and email service providers process email messages, these messages generate events that Twilio logs.

claims.value: Webhook data can be secured with Signed Event Webhook and/or OAuth 2.0
claims.quote: To secure the Event Webhook data, use the Signed Event Webhook, OAuth 2.0, or both.

claims.value: Official SDKs for C#, Go, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby
Free trial with no credit card required
claims.quote: Sign up for a free trial—no credit card required.
claims.verify_note: quote not found in fetched source text

claims.value: Community Twilio blog tutorial repo FINCH285/SendGrid-MCP-Server; the post is a contributor article, not an official release
claims.quote: The complete source code is available in this GitHub repository.

claims.value: No vendor-owned SendGrid MCP server confirmed
claims.quote: Opinions expressed by Twilio contributors are their own.

open_questions: Does the free/no-credit-card trial or free plan allow API calls and key creation without paying? Pricing pages did not load plan details (sendgrid.com/pricing redirected to twilio.com/en-us/sendgrid; the pricing product page was not fetched).
Is Basic auth with 'apikey' as username and key as password supported? Sources conflict; WebSearch summaries say both 'not supported' and 'supported for some services'.
Does the Event Webhook POST JSON, and is it ECDSA-signed? The page did not confirm transport or signing details.
Full endpoint list and read/write operations per resource: not established from fetched pages.

Official MCP: secondary sources conflict. One says Twilio runs an official docs server at mcp.twilio.com/docs (Public Beta, SendGrid spec search only). Another says SendGrid ships none. Not verified on Twilio's own pages or GitHub org. Check mcp.twilio.com and github.com/twilio-labs and github.com/sendgrid directly.

Community MCP servers found (not official): neschadin/sendgrid-mcp (MIT, states it is not affiliated with Twilio SendGrid), deyikong/sendgrid-mcp (58 tools, independent), coopersully/sendgrid-mcp, Garoth/sendgrid-mcp (Marketing API), @codespar/mcp-sendgrid on npm, FINCH285/SendGrid-MCP-Server (blog tutorial repo). Repos were listed in search results only, not fetched.
Fetch budget: about 8 page fetches used (two sendgrid.com/pricing redirects and one twilio.com redirect count), plus 2 searches.
SMTP is a separate sending protocol, not covered by the REST-only protocol field.

rationale: Self-serve test credentials (trial self serve) and a documented REST interface.
